Anas was serving his uncles a drink of ripe and unripe dates when alcohol was announced prohibited, and they told him to throw it away.
At night cover vessels, tie water-skins and shut doors naming Allah; do not drink from a water-skin's mouth or breathe into the vessel, and the Prophet took three breaths drinking.
Gold and silver vessels, like silk, are for unbelievers here, and drinking in silver fills the belly with Hell Fire; Sahl and Anas kept bowls the Prophet drank from.
At Asr, with only a little water in a vessel, water gushed from the Prophet's fingers and fourteen hundred men made ablution and drank from it.
Every hardship, sickness or thorn-prick expiates a Muslim's sins; the believer bends under trials like a tender plant, and the Prophet suffered double fever for a double reward.
Visit the sick, feed the hungry and free captives, the Prophet ordered; he and Abu Bakr walked to visit the unconscious Jabir, reviving him with his ablution water.
A black woman with epilepsy chose patience and Paradise over a cure, asking only not to be uncovered, and Allah promises Paradise to the patient who loses his sight.
Aisha visited the feverish Abu Bakr and Bilal; the Prophet visited a dying grandchild, a sick bedouin, a Jewish boy who embraced Islam and Sa'd, and was visited when ill.
Patients spoke of their pain: Ka'b's lice, Aisha's headache, the Prophet's high fever, and Sa'd's illness, when the Prophet said giving a third in charity was too much.
On his deathbed the Prophet offered to write a statement against going astray, but those present quarrelled after Umar said the Quran sufficed, and he sent them away.
Brought to the Prophet ill, the boy As-Sa'ib was blessed, drank the water of his ablution and saw the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders.
None should wish for death over a calamity, but ask to live while life is better; only the ban kept Khabbab from wishing it, and deeds alone earn none Paradise.
Resting against Aisha, the Prophet asked forgiveness, mercy and to join the highest companions; over the sick he asked the Lord of the people for a cure leaving no disease.
The Prophet revived the ill Jabir with his ablution water, and when Jabir, with no son or father to inherit, asked about his estate, the verse of inheritance was revealed.
After the emigration Abu Bakr and Bilal had fever, and the Prophet asked Allah to make Medina loved as Mecca or more, healthy and blessed, moving its fever to Al-Juhfa.
Allah created treatment for every disease; women on expeditions brought back the wounded; healing is in honey, cupping and cautery, which the Prophet disliked; honey cured abdominal trouble.
Sick men sent to drink the Prophet's camels' milk and urine recovered, killed his shepherd and drove off the camels; caught, they had hands and feet cut and eyes branded.
Black cumin heals every disease except death, talbina comforts the sick and grieving, and Indian incense treats seven diseases; the Prophet was cupped, paid the cupper and used snuff.
The Prophet was cupped while fasting and in ihram, on his head, paid the cupper and forbade pressing children's tonsils; Ka'b was told to shave his lice-ridden head and expiate.
Shown the nations, the Prophet was told seventy thousand of his followers will enter Paradise without reckoning: those avoiding Ruqya, omens and cautery who trust their Lord, Ukasha among them.
A widow with sore eyes may not use kohl; the Prophet said she keeps four months and ten days, unlike the former custom of a year in dirty clothes.
There is no 'Adwa, evil omen from birds, Hama or bad omen in Safar, yet one should run from a leper as one runs from a lion.
Truffle water heals the eyes; the Prophet had those who forced medicine into his mouth take it, had seven water-skins poured on him, and prescribed Indian incense and honey.
Told there is no 'Adwa, Safar or Hama, a bedouin asked about mange spreading among his camels, and the Prophet asked who infected the first one.
Indian incense cures seven diseases; Ruqya was allowed for poison and ear ailment; Anas was cauterised; Fatima's ash stopped the Prophet's bleeding; fever, from Hell's heat, is cooled with water.
Men of Ukl and Uraina, given camels' milk and urine to drink, reverted to disbelief, killed the shepherd and took the camels; their eyes were branded and hands cut off.
Do not enter or flee a plague-struck land, as Abdur-Rahman told Umar; plague will not enter Medina, and dying of it or enduring it patiently brings a martyr's reward.
The Prophet blew the Mu'auwidhat over himself when ill; Al-Fatiha recited as Ruqya earned sheep he approved; Ruqya treats the evil eye and stings, invoking the Lord of the people.
A good dream is from Allah and a bad one from Satan; whoever sees one he dislikes should blow thrice and seek refuge with Allah from its evil.
At bedtime the Prophet recited Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas and blew on his palms, wiping his body, as Aisha did for him when ill; Al-Fatiha cured a stung chief.
Seventy thousand of the Prophet's followers will enter Paradise without accounts: those who draw no evil omen, use no cautery or Ruqya and trust their Lord; Ukasha is one.
There is no 'Adwa, Tiyara, Hama or Safar, though an evil omen may be in a woman, house or animal; the best omen is the Fal, a good word.
When a Hudhail woman's stone killed another's unborn child, the Prophet judged a male or female slave as blood money, calling the objecting guardian a brother of soothsayers.
The Prophet forbade money from a dog's price, prostitution and fortune-telling; foretellers are nothing, passing on a word a jinn snatched, mixed with a hundred lies.
Labid bin Al-A'sam worked magic on the Prophet till Allah revealed it lay in Dharwan's well; avoid shirk and witchcraft; some eloquence works like magic; Ajwa dates guard against magic.
The Prophet denied 'Adwa, asking who infected the first mangy camel, yet barred mixing sick cattle with healthy; evil omen is only in horse, woman or house; he liked Fal.
After Khaibar's conquest the Prophet questioned the Jews about a poisoned roasted sheep given him; they admitted poisoning it to learn whether he was a liar or a prophet.
Whoever kills himself by throwing himself from a mountain, by poison or with an iron weapon will go on doing so in the Fire forever.
Seven Ajwa dates guard against magic and poison; fanged beasts are forbidden as food; a fly falling in a vessel is dipped wholly, one wing bearing disease, the other healing.
Allah will not look at one dragging his garment in pride; a proud man sank into the earth; Abu Bakr's slipping Izar was excused; the Prophet once hurried, dragging his.
